interpretation: All 78 time arrays are unmasked, finite, strictly increasing and have no duplicate timestamps. This does not imply complete velocity coverage.
All 78 coordinate records have singleton finite values within geographic bounds. A reviewed observation map and cross-instrument position consistency remain separate.
ADCP paired availability varies substantially. These are full-record paired unmasked finite velocity cells divided by all time-by-bin cells, not fractions of current area or physically valid flow.

Supplied ADCP depth arrays include negative minima. The audit did not impose a physical layer or verify that negative-depth cells contain paired velocity; use these as support diagnostics, not accepted water-column observations.
Point-meter pressure variation is retained in decibar and is not converted to moving depth. Nominal depth labels cannot define fixed observed layers.

Float64 days-since-1950 produces microsecond-scale offsets around nominal hourly/half-hourly times. Calendar-boundary normalization and cross-instrument synchronization need explicit rules in the later measurement method; the audit labels follow the decoded values without snapping.
No tides were removed, velocities rotated, observations interpolated, current identities joined, width edges selected or physical dimensions calculated.
remaining_requirements: Review physical QC and processing notes, including surface interference, depth validity and motion/blowdown.
Freeze timestamp normalization, synchronized overlap and common physical layer rules.
Resolve coastal versus slope/deep current identity and whether both velocity edges are observed.
Freeze width/edge/censoring and seasonal aggregation methods before deriving dimensions.
Verify an accessible observation-support viewer in a separate serialized cloud browser stage.
review_scope: One assistant reviewing exact successful cloud support results. No independent scientific peer review or current-measurement approval.
